subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should OpenClaw accept backup excludes with automatic `.backupignore` loading and partial external-asset semantics, or require a narrower explicit opt-in design before this feature can merge?
rationale: The PR changes backup recovery and security behavior, and automation cannot authorize the product/security tradeoff of silently reading state-local ignore files or leaving external assets outside the exclude contract.

options.title: Require narrowed rebase before merge
options.body: Ask for a rebased PR that makes `.backupignore` explicit or clearly approved, applies excludes across all backed-up assets, preserves current backup hardening, and includes real behavior proof.

options.title: Accept current semantics explicitly
options.body: Maintainership can choose to keep auto `.backupignore` and external-asset warning semantics, but that accepts compatibility and security-boundary risk for backup completeness.

options.title: Close and replace with smaller work
options.body: Close this stale conflicting branch and sponsor a smaller replacement PR for the canonical exclude-pattern issue.

recommendation.title: Require narrowed rebase before merge
recommendation.body: Ask for a rebased PR that makes `.backupignore` explicit or clearly approved, applies excludes across all backed-up assets, preserves current backup hardening, and includes real behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the local backup CLI surface most directly affected by this product decision.
